correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the entire centroidal profile and comparison. Horizontal slice area proportional to z gives centroid 2H/3; the plane graph Jacobian is R²√(1+κ²s²), and completing the square in normalized base coordinates gives a disk cut at u=1/(3s), tangent exactly at s=1/3. The vertical integral gives 4RH/3. For s>1/3, writing Fε(w)=√((2/3+w−εw²)₊) on [−2/3,1/3] with ε=s⁻² both proves the strict bound sS<4/3 and justifies the first variation: [F0−Fε]/ε is dominated by w²/√(2/3+w), with pointwise limit half that bound. The integral of the bound is 2/5, yielding T(∞)=5/3. The strict comparison after squaring is κ²<T(s), with equality exactly at κ²=T(s); T increases to contact, T(1/3)>3, and its right derivative at contact is positive. Thus the maximizers of T are contained in a compact subset of (1/3,∞). The finite maximizers near the switch on the oblique side also remain bounded, since having area greater than vertical requires T(s)>κ² and the limiting T is strictly below κ*². Contact depth has derivative 18/5 and disk radius 5/6; direct width integration gives the normalized loss coefficient 24√6/5 (Euclidean area loss also includes the smooth graph factor). Haar probability follows from uniform |N_z| and tan β=κs, with the stated scale inverse. Independently reproduced a numerical stationary candidate at s≈0.36724362585 and √T≈1.98151821145; that is corroboration only. The packaged checker was inspected, not executed; no certified decimal, uniqueness of finite maximizer, or formal verification is inferred.

value.rationale: This solves the natural orientation extremum over all centroidal planes for a basic nonsymmetric solid, throughout all aspect ratios. The finite-oblique/vertical coexistence and discontinuity are substantive, since they require a global comparison rather than identifying a tangency or performing a standard ellipse integral. The contact cusp and aspect-ratio inference add useful exact geometry but would not alone carry the value case.
